paper.title: Distributions of money in model markets of economy
paper.journal: International Journal of Modern Physics C 13(10):1315-1321

headline: Chakraborti 2002 Yard-Sale (agent-based): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; final Gini=0.993 (>>DY 0.5) with bottom-50% ~4e-46, but richest-agent share 0.27 < 0.90 at 2e4 sweeps (oligarchy, not yet single-winner) -> P2 MISS

verdicts.gate: P1 condensation: final Gini >= 0.95 on every seed AND the Gini(t) trajectory climbs monotonically toward 1
P2 oligarchy: the single richest agent holds >= 0.90 of total wealth AND the bottom 50% jointly hold <= 0.01
reasons: mean richest-agent share = 0.2741 over 10 seeds (range [0.203, 0.349]); need >= 0.9

at the locked 2e4-sweep budget wealth has condensed onto a small OLIGARCHY (a handful of agents), not yet a SINGLE winner; single-agent takeover to >=0.90 is the asymptotic limit but needs far more than 2e4 sweeps for N=1000

verdicts.gate: P3 distinct from the exponential: final Gini >= 0.70, well above the Dragulescu-Yakovenko exponential's 0.5 (condensation, not thermalization)

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce multiplicative wealth condensation (Gini->1, opposite the DY exponential's 0.5), isolate that it is the stake-the-poorer rule (not the conservation law) that condenses, and would catch an artifact

citations: Chakraborti, A. (2002). Distributions of money in model markets of economy. Int. J. Mod. Phys. C 13(10):1315-1321. doi:10.1142/S0129183102003905.
Hayes, B. (2002). Follow the Money. American Scientist 90(5):400-405.

Dragulescu, A. & Yakovenko, V.M. (2000). Statistical mechanics of money. Eur. Phys. J. B 17:723-729. (the additive-exchange exponential contrast).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the Gini, richest-agent share, and bottom-50% share of the conserved wealth vector
